question: A model's reply comes to about 300 tokens. Roughly how many times did the whole model run to produce it?

options.text: Once, because a single pass produces the entire reply
options.feedback: A single pass produces a single token, not a reply. Getting 300 tokens out of a one-token machine takes the loop of appending and re-running.

options.text: Twice, once to read the prompt and once to write the reply
options.feedback: Reading and writing are not separate phases. Every run reads the whole context, including the prompt, and writes exactly one token.

options.text: About a dozen times, roughly once per sentence
options.feedback: Sentences are not the model's unit of work. Each run yields one token, so the count of runs tracks tokens, not sentences.

options.text: About 300 times, once for each token
options.feedback: The model runs once per token, and each run takes the whole context, now one token longer. That is why a long reply takes noticeably longer than a short one.
